 ::Judgment:

:
The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.
SCCH 5 2.

The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 25.04.2022 at about 11.00 p.m. Prajwal S. Rao took the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KL-60-3920 of respondent No.2 for his work, when he was riding the said motor cycle on Mairakatte, Biliyooru Village, Bantwala Taluk, Dakshina Kannada, at that time, unknown lorry dashed against the said motor cycle, as a result Prajwal S.
Rao fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to First Neuro Hospital, Mangaluru, after firstaid then shifted to A.J.Hospital,
Mangaluru, but he succumbed to the fatal injuries on the way to the hospital.
3. At the time of accident, deceased/Prajwal S. Rao was aged about 21 years, doing catering work/student, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
petitioner is mother of the deceased.

The death of Prajwal S. Rao is arised out of use of motor cycle bearing Reg.
SCCH 5 No.KL-60-3920.
Respondent No.1 is insurer and respondent No.2 is R.C.Owner of the said motor cycle.
Respondent No.2 is close friend of the deceased, hence petitioners are entitled for personal accident coverage of Rs.15,00,000/- from respondent No.1.
Out of this accident, crime No.79/2022 is registered before the Puttur Traffic Police.
So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.54,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared through counsel and filed written statement.
Further submitted that, alleged vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and no charge sheet has been filed against the said motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KL-60-3920.

Further submitted that, deceased was not third party and there was no coverage to the deceased and no additional premium was paid and policy is only liability only policy for the coverage of the third SCCH 5 party risk only.

Further submitted that, this tribunal has no jurisdiction to entertain the Preethi Satheesh vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173065574/
2 petition of hit and run case and as per the police documents i.e., charge sheet, the offending vehicle has not traced, hence 'C' report has been filed, therefore petition under Sec.166 is not maintainable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further submitted that, petition is not maintainable for non-joinder of necessary party, as the offending lorry owner and insurer are not made as parties to the proceedings.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, it had issued insurance policy bearing No.3001013121P109602408 in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KL-60- 3920 and liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH 5 Respondent No.2/owner has appeared through counsel, but not chosen to file written statement.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, deceased Prajwal S. Rao died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.04.2022 at about 11.00 p.m. when deceased was riding a motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KL-60-3920 near Mairakatte, Biliyooru Village,
Bantwala Taluk, Dakshina Kannada, at that time, one knknown Lorry dashed against the said motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6.
In order to prove her case, petitioner/mother of the deceased herself deposed her evidence as PW-1 SCCH 5 and exhibited 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 and closed evidence.
On the other hand, Administrative Officer of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Negative  Issue No.2 : In the Negative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
Preethi Satheesh vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173065574/
3  :

sentences.text: : REASONS

: : 
8. Issue No.1 and 2:- As these issues are inter connected with each other, hence they have taken together to avoid repetition of same facts.
In order to SCCH 5 prove their case, petitioner/mother of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in her chief-examination she has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.

In this regard she has exhibited copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of P.M.Report is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of police intimation is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of mahazar is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.8 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.9.
9.

On perusal of the said documents including charge sheet marked as Ex.P.9 clearly indicates to the court that, i.e., 'C" Report has been filed against deceased Prajwal S. Rao for the alleged offence punishable under Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC, Sec.134(a & b) of M.V.Act.

Ofcourse during the course of arguments, respondent No.1 counsel Sri.KRS argued that, it is hit and run case SCCH 5 and MVC case is not maintainable and only Deputy Commissioner is proper jurisdiction to award compensation and Investigation Officer has filed 'C' Report and there is no charge sheet has been filed against the respondent No.2 insured vehicle and prays to dismiss the petition by relying on following rulings;
i) 2004 ACJ 645 in between Saroja and others V/s. General Insurance Corporation of India and others ii) 2005 ACJ 2105 in between Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Vidya Devi and others iii) 2024 ACJ 213 10.

entities.text: Saroja and others V/s. General Insurance Corporation of India and others ii) 2005 ACJ 2105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Vidya Devi and others iii) 2024 ACJ 213
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra counsel for petitioner argued that, deceased is a third party and rulings submitted by the respondent No.1 have not supports the present case and also citations produced by the respondent No.1 are pertaining to Sec.163A of M.V.Act and policy issued by the 1st respondent is valid for the date of the accident, SCCH 5 petitioners are claiming only personal accident damages of Rs.15,00,000/- and charge sheet is not required and this petition is maintainable and deceased step into the shoes of the owner, because owner has allowed the deceased to ply vehicle and prays to allow the petition etc.,

11. In the rulings of the respondent No.1, their lordships have held the following principles;
i) If any case arise out of hit and run accident, then MVC cases are not maintainable before the tribunals and Deputy Commissioner is competent person to award compensation.

ii) Incase of hit and run accident, Rs.25,000/- is admissible for death of the deceased as per Sec.161(3) (a) as amended in 1994 in view of beneficial nature of the legislation etc., SCCH 5 Preethi Satheesh vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173065574/
4 12.

entities.text: SCCH 5 Preethi Satheesh vs United India Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So as per the rulings of the 1st respondent, incase of hit and run accident, definitely petition under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is not maintainable.

Ofcourse there are some remedies under Sec.161(3)
and Solatium Scheme 1989, clauses 20, 22 and 23, but petitioner has not filed this petition under said provision and she claims compensation under Sec.166 of M.V.Act.

Admittedly as stated above,
there is no charge sheet has been filed in this case and 'C' Report has been filed against deceased Prajwal S. Rao.
So in the absence of filing of charge sheet and proof of negligency on the part of the respondent No.2 insured vehicle and further admittedly there is no vehicle has been traced out in this case.

Hence police have filed 'C' report in the present case on alleged complaint of the petitioner, that means on perusal of overall materials, there is no proof by the petitioner with regard to liability of 1st respondent for payment of SCCH 5 compensation as alleged in the petition and further as stated supra, in the absence of charge sheet against 1st respondent insured vehicle, merely police have filed 'C' Report and respondent No.1 has issued policy as per the petition are all not sufficient to allow the petition, because there is separate scheme has been provided as per the rulings of the respondent No.1, as such petitioner is at liberty to claim compensation before competent forums, that too present petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is not maintainable.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 and 2 in the negative.
13. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: :
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is hereby dismissed.
SCCH 5 Parties to bear their own costs.
Draw award accordingly.
